title: Tank stops filling at half level
summary: The tank should fill to 60 % but stops near 50 %, and the level display reads higher than the sight glass, most of all when the tank is nearly empty.
objectives: Check an analog signal from the transmitter to the engineering value
Find a configuration error with a measurement
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1 (normally open). *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2 (normally closed: TRUE while not pressed). *)
    LevelLow : BOOL; (* TRUE while the level is below the low switch (LSL-104 contact closes when dry). *)
    LevelHigh : BOOL; (* TRUE while the level is at or above the high switch (LSH-103 contact closes when wet). *)
    InletOpen : BOOL; (* Inlet valve fully-open limit switch. *)
    LevelRaw : INT; (* Raw analog value of LT-105 (scaling depends on the selected platform profile). *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    InletValve : BOOL; (* Inlet valve solenoid XV-101: TRUE opens the valve. *)
    DrainPump : BOOL; (* Drain pump P-102 contactor. *)
    LevelPercent : REAL; (* Level 0..100 % computed from LevelRaw *)
    HighAlarm : BOOL; (* Level above 85 % *)
END_VAR
VAR
    Filling : BOOL;
END_VAR

LevelPercent := INT_TO_REAL(LevelRaw) / 100.0;
HighAlarm := LevelPercent > 85.0;
Filling := (StartPB OR Filling) AND StopPB AND LevelPercent < 60.0 AND NOT HighAlarm;
InletValve := Filling;
DrainPump := FALSE;

END_PROGRAM
instructions: Compare LevelPercent with the real tank level in the Process view.
Measure the loop current at the analog input and calculate the expected percentage.
Inspect the analog channel configuration (Hardware, Advanced mode).
hints: A 4-20 mA transmitter delivers 5.6 mA at 10 % level.
What does a channel configured for 0-20 mA make of 4 mA?

criteria.title: LevelPercent matches the tank level
criteria.onFail: LevelPercent was not about 10 % while the tank was at 10 %. Check the scaling (generic profile: 0..10000 = 0..100 %).

criteria.title: The valve closes at 60 %
criteria.onFail: InletValve stayed open after the analog level reached 60 %.

troubleshooting.symptom: Filling stops at about half the tank instead of 60 %. The HMI shows 28 % when the sight glass shows 10 %.

diagnosisOptions.label: The analog input channel is configured for 0-20 mA instead of 4-20 mA
The program scales the raw value wrongly
The inlet valve closes too early

debrief.rootCause: The analog input channel was configured for 0-20 mA while the level transmitter delivers 4-20 mA. The channel turned the live-zero 4 mA into 20 % instead of 0 %, so every level read too high and filling stopped early.
evidence: At about 10 % real level the loop current measured 5.6 mA, which is exactly 10 % on a 4-20 mA scale.
On a 0-20 mA scale 5.6 mA becomes 28 %, the value the HMI showed.
The error was largest near empty and shrank toward full: a zero offset, not a gain or wiring problem.
The current was well above 0 mA and stable, which rules out a broken loop.
debrief.repair: Set the analog channel to 4-20 mA in the hardware configuration and download the station. No program change was needed.
debrief.reasoning: Measure the signal and calculate what the engineering value should be. When the measured current is right but the value is wrong, the fault is in the configuration or scaling between the terminal and the program, not in the transmitter.
